carlyle::Hexaware Technologies.notes: Hexaware Technologies is a real IT services company headquartered in Navi Mumbai. Carlyle acquired a majority stake (approx. 95%) in 2021. carlyle::Medline Industries.notes: Medline Industries (headquartered in Northfield, IL) was acquired in a $34 billion leveraged buyout in 2021 by a consortium including Carlyle, Blackstone, and Hellman & Friedman. carlyle::Nouryon.notes: Nouryon was acquired by Carlyle and GIC in 2018. As of February 2026, it remains a privately held portfolio company, with recent reports indicating that Carlyle is preparing for a potential IPO.

carlyle::Logoplaste.notes: Logoplaste is a real company headquartered in Cascais, Portugal, specializing in rigid plastic packaging. While it was a Carlyle portfolio company (Carlyle acquired a majority stake in 2016), Carlyle exited the investment in 2021 by selling its stake to the Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan (OTPP).

carlyle::Veritas.notes: Veritas Technologies was acquired by Carlyle in 2016. In December 2024, its core data protection business merged with Cohesity; Carlyle rolled over its interest and remains a major shareholder (approx. 21%) in the combined entity. The remaining assets (Arctera) were sold to Cloud Software Group in December 2025.

carlyle::Atotech.notes: Atotech was acquired by Carlyle from Total in 2017. After an IPO in 2021, Carlyle sold its remaining majority stake to MKS Instruments in August 2022, completing its exit.

carlyle::Ortho Clinical Diagnostics.notes: Ortho Clinical Diagnostics was acquired by Carlyle from Johnson & Johnson in 2014. Carlyle took the company public in 2021 and it was subsequently acquired by Quidel Corporation in May 2022 to form QuidelOrtho, marking Carlyle's exit.

carlyle::PPD.notes: PPD (Pharmaceutical Product Development), headquartered in Wilmington, NC, was acquired by Carlyle and Hellman & Friedman in 2011. carlyle::Beautycounter.notes: Carlyle acquired a majority stake in Beautycounter in April 2021 at a $1 billion valuation. It exited the investment in early 2024 by handing the company over to lenders (foreclosure) after significant financial decline. Founder Gregg Renfrew subsequently repurchased the brand's assets in April 2024.

carlyle::Fortitude Re.notes: Fortitude Re is a Bermuda-based reinsurance company. Carlyle (along with T&D Holdings) acquired a majority stake from AIG in 2020. As of early 2025, Carlyle remains a significant shareholder and strategic partner, continuing to manage assets and participate in capital raises for the company.

carlyle::Sedgwick.notes: Sedgwick is a Memphis-based global claims management provider. Carlyle acquired a majority stake in the company in 2018 for $6.7 billion. As of late 2024, Carlyle remains the controlling shareholder following a $1 billion minority investment from Altas Partners that valued the company at $13.2 billion.

carlyle::Neptune Energy.notes: Neptune Energy was co-founded and backed by Carlyle (holding a 30.6% stake) alongside CVC and CIC in 2015. The company, headquartered in London, was sold to Eni and Vår Energi in a transaction that completed in January 2024 for an enterprise value of approximately $4.9 billion.

carlyle::HireVue.notes: HireVue is a real company headquartered in South Jordan, Utah. carlyle::One Medical.notes: One Medical (1Life Healthcare) was a Carlyle portfolio company following a $350 million investment in 2018. Carlyle held a significant stake through its 2020 IPO and fully exited when Amazon acquired the company for $3.9 billion in February 2023.

carlyle::Flender.notes: Flender is a German industrial manufacturer headquartered in Bocholt. It was acquired by The Carlyle Group from Siemens in March 2021 for approximately €2 billion. As of early 2026, it remains a Carlyle portfolio company, although reports from late 2024 indicated that Carlyle was exploring exit options such as an IPO or sale.

carlyle::Mehiläinen.notes: Mehiläinen is a major Finnish healthcare company, but it is not owned by Carlyle. It is currently a portfolio company of CVC Capital Partners and Hellman & Friedman. It was previously owned by KKR and Triton Partners (2010–2018) and 3i (2006–2010).

carlyle::Rede D'Or.notes: Rede D'Or São Luiz is a major Brazilian healthcare provider. Carlyle first invested in the company in 2015 and fully exited its remaining stake in May 2024 through a block trade on the Brazilian stock exchange.

carlyle::SBI Card.notes: Carlyle (via CA Rover Holdings) acquired a 26% stake in SBI Card from GE Capital in December 2017. It began paring its stake during the company's IPO in March 2020 and completed its exit in April 2022 by selling its remaining 3.09% stake.

carlyle::PA Consulting.notes: PA Consulting was a portfolio company of Carlyle from 2015 until March 2021, when Carlyle exited its stake following a majority investment by Jacobs Engineering Group (now Jacobs Solutions).

carlyle::Novolex.notes: Novolex is a packaging manufacturer headquartered in Hartsville, South Carolina. carlyle::ZoomInfo.notes: ZoomInfo (formerly DiscoverOrg) was a Carlyle portfolio company following a minority investment in 2018. The company went public in June 2020 (NASDAQ: ZI). carlyle::Included Health.notes: Included Health is a San Francisco-based healthcare company formed by the 2021 merger of Grand Rounds and Doctor On Demand. carlyle::Piramal Pharma.notes: Piramal Pharma Limited is a Mumbai-based pharmaceutical company. The Carlyle Group acquired a 20% stake in the company in 2020 for approximately $490 million. carlyle::iCIMS.notes: iCIMS is a real company headquartered in Holmdel, NJ. carlyle::TriNetX.notes: The Carlyle Group acquired a majority stake in TriNetX in September 2020 through its Carlyle Partners VII fund. The company is headquartered in Cambridge, MA, and operates in the healthcare technology sector. It remains a current portfolio company of Carlyle.

carlyle::Saama Technologies.notes: Saama Technologies is a real company headquartered in Campbell, California. In October 2021, funds led by Carlyle acquired a majority stake in the company for approximately $430 million. As of early 2026, Carlyle remains the majority owner and the company is still part of its portfolio.

carlyle::Net Health.notes: Net Health is a Pittsburgh-based healthcare technology company. It was acquired by The Carlyle Group (specifically through its U.S. Equity Opportunity Fund II) in December 2017, alongside Level Equity and Silversmith Capital Partners. As of February 2026, it remains a current portfolio company.

carlyle::Dept.notes: Dept (DEPT®) is a digital agency headquartered in Amsterdam. The Carlyle Group acquired a majority stake in the company in early 2020 (announced Dec 2019). As of late 2025, it remains a portfolio company of Carlyle, with industry reports discussing its growth and potential future exit options such as an IPO.

carlyle::EUSA Pharma.notes: EUSA Pharma is a real company headquartered in Hemel Hempstead, UK. However, it was a portfolio company of EW Healthcare Partners (formerly Essex Woodlands), not Carlyle. While Carlyle's AlpInvest unit is a minority co-investor in Recordati (which is majority-owned by CVC Capital Partners), EUSA Pharma itself was never a Carlyle portfolio company.

carlyle::SeQuent Scientific.notes: Carlyle acquired a majority stake (up to 74%) in SeQuent Scientific in 2020. As of late 2024 and early 2025, Carlyle remains the promoter and majority shareholder. The company is currently undergoing a merger with Viyash Life Sciences, another Carlyle portfolio company.

carlyle::Quest Global.notes: Quest Global is a Singapore-headquartered engineering services firm. Carlyle acquired a significant minority stake (approx. 24-28%) in August 2023, marking its second investment in the company. As of February 2026, Carlyle remains a major shareholder alongside founder Ajit Prabhu.

carlyle::CorroHealth.notes: CorroHealth is a healthcare technology company headquartered in Plano, TX. Carlyle has been a majority investor since 2019 and, following a strategic investment from Patient Square Capital in late 2024, currently shares joint control of the company.

carlyle::Adare Pharma Solutions.notes: Adare Pharma Solutions is a real specialty CDMO headquartered in Lawrenceville, NJ. It is currently a portfolio company of Thomas H. carlyle::YipitData.notes: YipitData is a New York-based alternative data and technology company. advent-international::Parfums de Marly.notes: Advent International acquired a majority stake in Parfums de Marly (and its sister brand Initio Parfums Privés) in June 2023. advent-international::Zimmermann.notes: Advent International acquired a majority stake in the Sydney-based luxury fashion brand Zimmermann in August 2023 from Style Capital. It remains a current portfolio company as of early 2025.

advent-international::Sovos Brands.notes: Sovos Brands was founded by Advent International in 2017 and remained a portfolio company (including after its 2021 IPO) until it was acquired by Campbell Soup Company in March 2024 for $2.7 billion. It is headquartered in Louisville, Colorado.

advent-international::First Watch.notes: First Watch (FWRG) was acquired by Advent International in 2017 and went public in October 2021. Advent progressively reduced its stake through secondary offerings, fully divesting its remaining 8.7% stake in November 2025.

advent-international::Bojangles.notes: Bojangles was acquired by Advent International in 2011 and taken public in 2015. In 2019, the company was acquired and taken private by The Jordan Company and Durational Capital Management, meaning it is no longer in Advent's portfolio.

advent-international::Encora.notes: Encora is a digital engineering services company headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona. advent-international::Xplor Technologies.notes: Xplor Technologies was formed in 2021 by Advent International through the merger of two of its portfolio companies, Clearent and TSG. advent-international::Aareon.notes: Aareon is a real technology company headquartered in Mainz, Germany. While TPG is now the majority owner, Advent International retained a minority equity stake in the standalone company, meaning it is still currently held in their portfolio.

advent-international::Mangopay.notes: Mangopay is a Luxembourg-based fintech company acquired by Advent International in April 2022. As of early 2025, it remains a majority-owned portfolio company of Advent International, with Crédit Mutuel Arkéa retaining a minority stake.

advent-international::Ebury.notes: Ebury is a real fintech company headquartered in London, but it is not a portfolio company of Advent International. advent-international::Medline.notes: Medline Industries (headquartered in Northfield, IL) was acquired in 2021 by a consortium consisting of Blackstone, Carlyle, and Hellman & Friedman. advent-international::Orveon.notes: Orveon (Orveon Global) was established in December 2021 by Advent International to acquire and manage the bareMinerals, BUXOM, and Laura Mercier brands from Shiseido. It is headquartered in New York and remains a current portfolio company of Advent International in the consumer goods/beauty sector.

advent-international::Caldic.notes: Advent International acquired Caldic in March 2022 from Goldman Sachs Asset Management. advent-international::GfK.notes: GfK (headquartered in Nuremberg) merged with NielsenIQ (NIQ) in 2023. It is currently a portfolio company of Macquarie Asset Management (specifically through Macquarie European Infrastructure Fund 5) and Goldman Sachs Asset Management, which have each held a 50% stake since acquiring the company from Carlyle and Riverstone in 2019. Recent reports from late 2024 and 2025 confirm this ownership structure remains in place.

macquarie::Last Mile Infrastructure.notes: Last Mile Infrastructure is a UK-based utility network owner headquartered in Hamilton. Macquarie Asset Management (via its European Infrastructure Fund 7) acquired a 50% stake in the company in 2024 and announced a binding agreement in February 2026 to acquire the remaining 50% from Infracapital, moving to 100% ownership.

macquarie::Cero Generation.notes: Cero Generation was launched in February 2021 by Macquarie's Green Investment Group (GIG) and remains a portfolio company of Macquarie Asset Management (MAM). It is a specialist solar energy developer headquartered in London.

macquarie::Blueleaf Energy.notes: Blueleaf Energy is a Singapore-based pan-Asian renewable energy platform. It is a portfolio company owned by a fund managed by Macquarie Asset Management (MAM), having been developed through Macquarie's Green Investment Group (GIG). Recent reports from late 2025 confirm it remains under Macquarie's ownership and is actively expanding its operations.

macquarie::Guzman y Gomez.notes: Guzman y Gomez (GYG) is a real Australian-based Mexican fast-food chain, but it is not a portfolio company of Macquarie. It was primarily backed by TDM Growth Partners and Barrenjoey Capital Partners (which bought Magellan Financial Group's stake in 2022) before listing on the ASX in June 2024 (ASX: GYG). Macquarie Group provides analyst coverage and hosts the company at its conferences, but has no record of private equity ownership.

macquarie::Daesung Industrial Gases.notes: Daesung Industrial Gases (renamed DIG Airgas under Macquarie's ownership) was acquired by Macquarie from MBK Partners in 2020. In August 2025, Macquarie signed an agreement to sell the company to Air Liquide, completing the exit by late 2025.

macquarie::Brussels Airport.notes: Macquarie (via its MEIF1 and MEIF3 funds) acquired a stake in Brussels Airport in 2004 and completed its exit in December 2019 by selling its 36% interest to a consortium of APG, QIC, and Swiss Life.

macquarie::Vantage Towers.notes: Vantage Towers is a real company headquartered in Düsseldorf, but it is a portfolio company of Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) and KKR, not Macquarie. The two PE firms co-control the company alongside Vodafone through a vehicle called Oak Holdings. Macquarie has provided debt financing to a different entity, Vantage Data Centers, which may be the source of the confusion.

macquarie::Netcity.notes: Netcity Telecom is a real company operating Bucharest's underground fiber optic network. It is owned by the Romanian holding E-INFRA (through Direct One) and the French asset manager Meridiam, which acquired a 50% stake in 2021. While Macquarie is a major infrastructure investor in Romania (having acquired CEZ Group's Romanian assets in 2020), it does not own Netcity.
